pr_title: Don't apply max_frag_len checking if no Max Fragment Length extension
pr_body:
Don't check the Max Fragment Length if the it hasn't been negotiated. We
were checking it anyway, and using the default value
(SSL3_RT_MAX_PLAIN_LENGTH). This works in most cases but KTLS can cause the
record length to actually exceed this in some cases.

Fixes https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/23169

While investigating this I encountered a build error on FreeBSD if KTLS is enabled, so I have fixed that too.

The test is tentative. I expected the test would reproduce the failure - but it didn't. I currently don't know under what conditions the failure occurs.
pr_comments: I've taken this out of draft - please review. I still can't replicate the problem directly, but the reporter has confirmed that this fixes the issue. The test does not seem to trigger the problem - but it does no harm to have it there anyway.
This pull request is ready to merge

issue_context.title: KTLS RX issues in 3.2.0+
issue_context.body:
After upgrading openssl from 3.0.x to 3.2.0 or master we are running into an error in a simple SSL_read() loop if KTLS is used for receiving.

error:0A000092:SSL routines::data length too long

I tracked this down to ssl/record/methods/tls_common.c and method tls_get_more_records.

The code there :
```
        /*
         * Check if the received packet overflows the current
         * Max Fragment Length setting.
         * Note: rl->max_frag_len > 0 and KTLS are mutually exclusive.
         */

        if (thisrr->length > rl->max_frag_len) {
            RLAYERfatal(rl, SSL_AD_RECORD_OVERFLOW, SSL_R_DATA_LENGTH_TOO_LONG);
            goto end;
        }
```

In my case the record length is 16688 and max_frag_len is the same as SSL3_RT_MAX_PLAIN_LENGTH.
It seems these checks are treated in a special way in 3.0.x for KTLS. See :
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/17504

Seems to me this got reintroduced in refactoring for 3.2.0 ?
comments:
I can confirm the patch fixes the issue.

I had the issue on Linux (I couldn't build on fbsd either but I thought that was my fault somehow). Even tried various kernel versions as I thought it might be a kernel issue. Currently replicating it on Ubuntu 23.10.

The program is an FTP server and it's possible to actually replicate it on every single file upload. The server just opens a new connection for the upload and after the SSL_connect/SSL_accept it just loops the SSL_read. I'm doing the upload from localhost and using 8 MB file. Happens both with normal SSL_write loop and SSL_sendfile.

review_comments: Given the documentation language above, specifically "Also not that with KTLS thisrr->length can be > SSL3_RT_MAX_PLAIN_LENGTH (and rl->max_frag_len must be ignored).  Given that, shouldn't this check be reversed so that thisrr->length is checked first, and rl->max_frag_len is only interrogated if the former is > SSL3_RT_MAX_PLAIN_LENGTH?

Not really sure why? It makes more sense to me this way. Checking `max_frag_len != SSL3_RT_MAX_PLAIN_LENGTH` is a test to see if max_frag_len has been negotiated or not. The second part is a test to see if the max_frag_len has been exceeded. In other words we are saying "if max_frag_len has been negotiated and it has been exceeded then error". Doing it the other way around says "if max_frag_len has been exceeded and it has been negotiated then error" - which seems somewhat nonsensical to me (if it hasn't been negotiated, then checking if it has been exceeded is meaningless).
